C1.text: Cedar uses an adaptive controller with a synchronized clock. The -Clock variant removes the synchronized clock while retaining the adaptive controller. We observed occasional timing jitter for Cedar when crowded channels delayed clock messages. We hypothesize that delayed clock messages may contribute to this jitter under those conditions; the experiment does not establish a sole cause.

C2.text: Birch is a different fixed-schedule method. Birch cannot adapt its schedule after initialization. This restriction is about Birch, not Cedar. Removing the clock in the -Clock variant reduced synchronization work but sometimes increased jitter; this does not show that Cedar cannot adapt.
